content:
At last night's Emmy Awards ceremony, Apple TV+ delivered an outstanding performance, beating rivals like HBO to become the most awarded platform of the night. Below is HBO's Casey Bloys' response to Apple TV+'s win.

HBO's CEO praised Apple TV+'s excellent performance while also acknowledging that competing against a trillion-dollar company is "quite challenging."

Apple TV+ has long been compared to HBO, with both prioritizing quality over quantity. Apple has even occasionally been called "the new HBO."

Last night's Emmys further cemented this notion, as Apple TV+ surpassed HBO, Netflix, and other platforms to become the most awarded platform of the night.

Apple TV+ took home a total of 29 awards, earning the title of "most awarded network of the year," with shows like *Widow's Bay* standing out in particular. HBO came in second with 21 awards.

After the Emmy ceremony ended, HBO executive Casey Bloys sat down with Deadline and was asked for his thoughts on Apple TV+'s performance. Here's what he said:

DEADLINE: What do you make of Apple TV+'s performance this time? They became the most awarded platform at the Emmys for the first time—is there anything you'd like to say? BLOYS: I'm actually really happy, because I think they're strong competitors—Zack and Jamie. We've always had strong competitors—Showtime, FX, AMC, Netflix, Amazon—so having Apple in the mix keeps everyone on their toes, and that's exactly when I perform at my best. They're a trillion-dollar company, so that is indeed a big challenge, but we'll keep doing what we've always done, which is making the best shows possible.

Bloys joined HBO in 2004 and has been in charge of programming since 2016. His track record speaks for itself, and his response to Apple TV+'s win was largely gracious and sincere in offering his congratulations.

However, the most interesting part of his response was this line: "They're a trillion-dollar company, so that is indeed a big challenge."

We don't know Apple TV+'s internal budget, but there's no question that Apple's overall financial resources far exceed those of most competitors, including HBO.

Coincidentally, Paramount is currently actively pursuing a takeover of HBO (along with other Warner Bros. Discovery assets), hoping to compete more effectively with tech giants like Apple and Amazon.

Does scale naturally bring advantage? Perhaps. But many networks have already proven that when it comes to producing content audiences love, money is only a small part of the equation.

Apple TV+ costs US$14.99 per month, and is also available as part of the Apple One subscription bundle.
